source.title: Guidelines on Ethical Advertising and Public Communication by Hospitals/Medical Institutions and Registered Medical Practitioners
source.issuer: National Medical Commission, Ethics & Medical Registration Board

footnote: * Internal working guide prepared by Digilantern from NMC Public Notice No. R-13014/01/2024-Ethics dated 06/10/2026. It is not legal advice. Items marked “Our interpretation” are not stated in the NMC document. Please have legal counsel review this guide before relying on it.

whatChanged.t: On 6 October 2026 NMC issued guidelines on advertising and public communication by doctors and clinics. They apply immediately.
Websites, ads, social media, influencer content, blogs, WhatsApp and AI content count as advertising whenever they are promotional.
Not allowed: testimonials, before-and-after photos, “best / No.1” claims, success rates, patient counts, endorsements, and inducement-style offers.
Doctor name, qualifications and registration number must show on electronic posts.
The penalty falls on the doctor, and using an agency does not remove that responsibility.
So every deliverable for a healthcare client now needs a check.

actionTypes.name: Remove
actionTypes.help: Take it down. The document prohibits it, and we have no compliant version of it.

actionTypes.name: Stop doing
actionTypes.help: Stop the practice or switch the feature off.

actionTypes.name: Rewrite
actionTypes.help: Keep the page or asset, but change the wording or design.

actionTypes.name: Add disclosure
actionTypes.help: Keep the content and add the required identity, AI or relationship details.

actionTypes.name: Verify
actionTypes.help: Check evidence, status or consent first, then keep, change or remove.

do: Share factual clinic information: name, address, contact, departments, facilities, accreditation, fees (§8.3(i), §9.1)
Show the doctor's name, qualifications, registration status and SMR/NMR number on electronic posts (§3.2 Expl. III–IV)
Publish genuinely educational, non-promotional health information (§3.2 Expl. I, §5.1)
Describe equipment as a fact, with no superiority or outcome claim (§3.2 Expl. II)
Label AI-generated promotional content with an AI source mark (§7.2)
Get written client approval for every change (§4.4)
dont: No testimonials, reviews as promotion, or influencer or celebrity endorsements (§3.2 Expl. V, §8.1(xi))
No before-and-after photos, surgical results or success stories (§8.1(v))
No success rates or patient counts; no “guaranteed”, “painless”, “miracle” (§8.1(iii))
No discounts, contests, coupons or free-procedure offers that induce care (§8.1(x))
No identifiable patient faces, names or marks, even with consent for a prohibited use (§6.2, §7.4)

covers: Everything the NMC notice states, mapped clause by clause. All 12 sections of the Guidelines and the cover notice are in the clause index.
Our recommended working practice for each of our deliverable types, labelled “Our interpretation”.
limits: The NMC document does not mention SEO, Google Ads mechanics (keywords, dynamic keyword insertion, extensions), retargeting, hashtags, review replies or review widgets. Where we give guidance on these it is our interpretation, and the grey-areas page lists them.
NMC may issue clarifications and SOPs later (§12). Check for them regularly.
State Medical Councils and State Clinical Establishments Acts may add their own rules (§4.2, §4.3). This guide does not cover them.
